raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: Oh, hi. Did you get a call from me?
ParticipantB: Yeah, just a minute ago. Yeah.
ParticipantA: Okay. So, the topic is family life. Right?
ParticipantB: Yeah, family stuff. Kids mostly.
ParticipantA: Oh, good. I have two. A girl, eight years old, and a boy, five.
ParticipantB: Oh, wow. That's young. I have one. Just a girl, three.
ParticipantA: Three? Okay. That's... that's the tough part I guess.
ParticipantB: Yeah, the little one. She's not even in school yet.
ParticipantA: Right. I feel like I'm just running from one to the other all day.
ParticipantB: Yeah, it's a full time job, for sure. Especially if you're driving a bus.
ParticipantA: Wait, you drive a bus?
ParticipantB: Yeah, school bus. It's my job.
ParticipantA: Oh, wow. That's intense. I'm an electrician.
ParticipantB: Really? That sounds cool. I mean, I've always liked it, but...
ParticipantA: What about it?
ParticipantB: Well, my cousin was an electrician too. And he... he didn't really like it.
ParticipantA: Oh? Why not? I thought you'd think it was great.
ParticipantB: He said it was too much stress. And the hours. And you know, you're always on call.
ParticipantA: Hmm. Yeah, I get that a lot. But I like the work itself.
ParticipantB: Really? Your cousin hated the work.
ParticipantA: No, no. My cousin was scared of heights maybe? Or something.
ParticipantB: Oh. Well, I guess everyone is different.
ParticipantA: Yeah. I've wanted to be an electrician since I was like... twelve?
ParticipantB: That's young to decide.
ParticipantA: I don't know why. Just felt like it was the only thing that made sense.
ParticipantB: Maybe because you're good with your hands?
ParticipantA: Maybe. I guess so. But sometimes I wonder if I made the right choice.
ParticipantB: You know, my daughter... she wants to be a vet.
ParticipantA: Oh, that's nice. That's very different from driving a bus.
ParticipantB: Yeah. She loves animals. But I tell her, "You gotta eat first."
ParticipantA: Haha. That's true. You can't have animals without money.
ParticipantB: Exactly. So I'm trying to keep the bus route safe and stable.
ParticipantA: Oh, that's important. Safety first.
ParticipantB: Yeah. I drive the same route for ten years. Same kids, same houses.
ParticipantA: That's nice. Some consistency. My kids go to different schools.
ParticipantB: Oh? Why?
ParticipantA: Well, we moved. The house had a bad wire. I had to fix it.
ParticipantB: Wait, what? You fixed your own house?
ParticipantA: Yeah. Did some rewiring myself. Saved some cash.
ParticipantB: Wow. I'd never do that. Too risky.
ParticipantA: Maybe. But it saved me money. And I liked figuring it out.
ParticipantB: I guess. My cousin said it's dangerous work.
ParticipantA: It is. But you learn. You learn what works.
ParticipantB: Yeah. My daughter... she's asking me about fixing things too.
ParticipantA: Oh? That's good. Tell her she can help.
ParticipantB: She does. She helped me fix the toy car last week.
ParticipantA: Nice! What did you fix?
ParticipantB: The wheel came loose. Just tightened it up.
ParticipantA: That's pretty cool. She's smart.
ParticipantB: Yeah. But she's also... she doesn't like school much.
ParticipantA: Oh? Why not?
ParticipantB: She says it's boring. Too many rules.
ParticipantA: Haha. My son feels the same sometimes.
ParticipantB: Yeah. He's five. So maybe he'll grow out of it.
ParticipantA: Maybe. Or maybe I'll just let him be an electrician too.
ParticipantB: Oh, really? That's your plan?
ParticipantA: Maybe. It's just... I like it. Too much to give up.
ParticipantB: I guess. But you know, I'm not sure it's the best for everyone.
ParticipantA: I know. But I like it. I like seeing the work done.
ParticipantB: Yeah. It is satisfying, I guess.
ParticipantA: Yeah. Like finishing a job.
ParticipantB: Right. I get to see kids safe on the bus. That's good too.
ParticipantA: Oh, that's great. You make them feel secure.
ParticipantB: Yeah. I hope they do.
ParticipantA: Well, I guess we're both doing our thing.
ParticipantB: Yeah. Different paths.
ParticipantA: But both good. I think.
ParticipantB: Yeah. I think so too.
ParticipantA: Okay. Well, I'm gonna go fix a ceiling fan.
ParticipantB: Oh? Did it break?
ParticipantA: No. Just thought I'd try to balance the blades.
ParticipantB: Nice. Maybe your daughter will want to help later.
ParticipantA: Maybe. She's busy right now anyway.
ParticipantB: Yeah. Well, I should get back to the depot.
ParticipantA: Okay. Same here.
ParticipantB: Take care.
ParticipantA: You too. Bye.
ParticipantB: Bye.
